name: Audit Chain
description: Tamper-evident, hash-chained audit logging for any Drupal module — optional HMAC signing, at-rest encryption, prefix seal for historical segments, and independent verification.
project_description: Tamper-evident audit logging for Drupal, usable by any module. Each entry's hash (HMAC-SHA256, or plain SHA-256 when unkeyed) covers its own content plus the previous entry's hash, so any later insertion, deletion or edit breaks the chain and is detectable by an independent verification pass. With a Key-module HMAC key configured, forging a repair also requires the key, so a database-level edit cannot be quietly papered over. Consumers write through Drupal\audit_chain\AuditChainLoggerInterface (service audit_chain.logger) identifying themselves by a channel; a request-scoped collector deduplicates high-frequency events and flushes once at kernel.terminate. Metadata can be encrypted at rest via an Encrypt profile. Drush commands verify the chain (exit code is the contract), seal an unverifiable historical prefix without re-chaining it, re-encrypt metadata across profiles, and export data-minimized NDJSON evidence off-system; cron can run scheduled verification and gated export. Extracted from MCP Sentinel, where it began as the audit trail for AI-agent traffic.
